papers.title_en: Neuromorphic Decision Dynamics for Deadlock-free Safe Navigation in Congested Environments
papers.authors: Himani Sinhmar, Vaibhav Srivastava, Naomi Ehrich Leonard
papers.evidence: 去中心化无死锁多智能体解冲突与协调通行
papers.tldr: 拥挤环境安全导航需同时避碰与协调通行，但现有方法常依赖通信、优先级或邻居模型。本文提出神经形态决策动力学NDD，一种去中心化事件驱动控制器，将内部决策与注意状态耦合局部相对运动，按冲突程度连续调速并自组织分组解冲突。理论分析给出感知范围、反馈增益、响应时间与执行限制条件，保证有限时间避碰和通行顺序形成，无死锁/活锁且可扩展。大规模仿真、对比与硬件实验验证其在复杂拥挤场景中的有效性与可扩展性。
papers.abstract_en: Safe navigation in congested environments requires both collision avoidance and coordinated passage. We introduce neuromorphic decision dynamics (NDD), a decentralized, event-based controller, that provides navigation in congested spaces with guarantees on safety, liveness, robustness, and scalability. NDD makes safe-and-live deconfliction a controllable, locally tunable emergent property of local agent interactions, without requiring communication, preassigned priorities, models of neighbors' objectives or future actions, or estimates of group size or global network properties. By design, NDD couples the dynamics of internal decision and attention states with changing physical states and locally observed relative motion. Each agent continuously modulates its speed along its prescribed path, responding as soon and as much as conflict resolution requires. Agents self-organize into disjoint, locally engaged groups that resolve conflicts concurrently. When any group's conflict becomes safety-critical, decision-action feedback destabilizes collective indecision, and coordinated conflict-resolution emerges that stabilizes a safe traversal order within the group. Order persists as conflicts clear, but groups may split or merge as agents autonomously adapt to new conflicts and those with resolved conflicts resume their nominal motion. We derive explicit conditions on sensing range, feedback gains, response time scales, and actuation limits that guarantee collision avoidance and traversal-order formation in finite time with no deadlock or livelock for finite, heterogeneous agent populations of arbitrary, changing size. Computational cost scales with the number of local interactions sensed by each agent. Large-scale simulations, comparisons with existing approaches, and hardware experiments demonstrate NDD in complex congested scenarios and validate its scalability.

papers.title_en: HA-DiPO: Diffusion Policy Optimization for Heterogeneous Cooperative Transport
papers.authors: Xuebin Li, Jinpeng Xiao, Zong Chen, Pierluigi Arpenti, Bruno Siciliano, Jiebao Sun, Yiqun Li
papers.evidence: 异构机器人团队的分层多智能体协调
papers.tldr: 针对异构腿式机器人协同搬运非固定共享负载时运动能力差异与协调难题，提出分层多智能体强化学习框架HA-DiPO。高层用集中式评论家与扩散协调策略联合训练，低层由各具身运动策略跟踪指令，执行时仅依赖局部观测且无需演示或机器人间通信。仿真中最终平均回报、速度跟踪成功率更高且速度误差更低，并完成四足-轮腿与人体-机器人实物协同搬运。
papers.abstract_en: Cooperative transport with heterogeneous legged robots requires coordinating different motion capabilities while supporting an unfixed shared payload. We present HA-DiPO (Heterogeneous-Agent Diffusion Policy Optimization), a hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning framework under centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE). The framework decouples team-level coordination from embodiment-specific motion control: at the high level, a centralized critic uses team-value estimates to jointly train independent coordination policies, aligning robot-specific action responses with a shared transport objective; at the low level, embodiment-specific robust motion policies track the coordination commands. The high-level diffusion policies offer more flexible action distributions than single-Gaussian parameterizations, allowing potentially multimodal coordination responses to be represented. The coordination policies learn from scratch through reward-driven simulator interaction without demonstrations. At execution, each robot generates coordination commands using only local robot and payload observations, without partner-state inputs or inter-robot messages. Simulation comparisons show that HA-DiPO achieves higher final mean returns and velocity-tracking success rates, as well as lower velocity errors, than the evaluated baselines. Real-world experiments further demonstrate quadrupedal-wheeled-legged and human-robot cooperative transport.

papers.title_en: MATE-BT: A Behavior-Tree-Based Framework for Hierarchically Decentralized Mission Autonomy in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Teams
papers.authors: Sunbeen Lee, Hoseon Gi, Jik Hur, Inmo Jang
papers.evidence: 异构多机器人团队的分层去中心化任务自治
papers.tldr: 异构多机器人执行预设任务时需应对运行期目标变化和机器人故障。MATE-BT 将任务推进、任务分配与本地执行分层解耦，由可转移的主动领导者管理团队级分配，各机器人用行为树进行规划与行动。Webots 仿真和实机实验验证了新目标及领导者失效下的任务连续性，30 个机器人、120 个目标时响应约 130 ms。该框架支持全板载计算，并在 Jetson Orin Nano 与 Raspberry Pi 5 上完成资源验证。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-robot teams executing predefined missions must adapt to runtime changes and sustain mission management despite robot failures. This paper proposes MATE-BT (Mission, Allocation, and Task Execution with Behavior Trees), a hierarchically decentralized framework that separates mission execution, allocation, and task execution. An active onboard leader manages mission progression and team-level task assignment, with authority transferable to another leader-capable robot after failure. Interchangeable decentralized methods resolve target assignments, while each robot adapts its local behavior through planning and acting with behavior trees. Webots simulations and real-robot experiments demonstrate mission continuity despite new targets and robot failures, including active-leader failure. In the physical experiments, all MATE-BT computation runs onboard. Hardware-in-the-loop resource measurements further support onboard execution on Jetson Orin Nano and Raspberry Pi 5. By updating only the affected layers without full-plan regeneration, MATE-BT maintained a response time of approximately 130 ms with 30 robots and 120 targets. Comparisons of four target-assignment plugins reveal scenario-dependent trade-offs between mission completion time and total travel distance.

papers.title_en: DSGN: A Dual-Stream Gated Network for Scalable Simultaneous Surveillance and Containment
papers.authors: Heng Zhang, Ziyang Zuo, Guoxiang Zhao, Xiaoqiang Ren
papers.evidence: 多机器人同时监视与围捕的协调
papers.tldr: 多机器人同时监视与围堵中，覆盖需要空间分散而围堵需要向目标聚拢，二者冲突使启发式切换不稳定，且随规模增大更明显。本文提出双流门控网络DSGN，将监视与围堵分到专用表征流，并用上下文感知门控协调，辅以概率先验正则化切换。恒定密度跨尺度实验表明DSGN保持较强任务效能与可扩展性，消融和阶段评估验证动态门控与先验有助任务仲裁和模式切换。
papers.abstract_en: The simultaneous surveillance and containment (SSC) problem arises in multi-robot applications such as perimeter security and environmental monitoring, where robots must survey a region of interest and coordinate to enclose targets once they are detected. Surveillance favors spatial dispersion for coverage, whereas containment requires target-centric cohesion for enclosure. This conflict makes heuristic switching unstable, and the instability becomes more pronounced as larger robotic networks introduce more inter-agent and agent-target relations. End-to-end DRL reduces reliance on hand-crafted switching, but conventional single-stream policies often mix surveillance and containment cues in one shared feature space that could entangle dispersion-oriented and target-centric signals and weaken task transitions. In this paper, we propose the Dual-Stream Gated Network (DSGN), an architecture designed to address scale-amplified task-transition difficulties by separating surveillance and containment into specialized representation streams and coordinating them through a context-aware gating mechanism. A probabilistic prior further regularizes the gating process, reducing ambiguous intermediate decisions and supporting clearer behavioral transitions under large-scale interaction complexity. Evaluations show that DSGN maintains strong task efficacy and scalability under constant-density cross-scale settings. Additional ablation and phase-specific evaluations show that the proposed dynamic gating mechanism and probabilistic prior support effective task arbitration and reliable mode switching in both pure surveillance and task-switching scenarios. The source code is available at https://github.com/zuozysama/DSGN.

papers.title_en: Distributed Predictive Flocking for a Swarm of Miniature Vibration-Driven Robots in a Confined Arena
papers.authors: Prajol Shrestha, Siddhant Mohapatra, Filip Novkoski, Julian Oelhaf, Nicolas Vandewalle, Ana-Sunčana Smith, Andreas Maier
papers.evidence: 分布式多机器人集群协调与避碰
papers.tldr: 针对受限场地内无领导者、无全局地图的微型机器人集群协调难题，提出分布式预测集群控制器：各机器人独立求解NMPC，仅与局部邻居交换预测轨迹，并融合凝聚、对齐、避碰与任务目标。在0.64平方米场地的振动驱动机器人数字孪生上比较六种安全约束，优选出前瞻离散时间CBF。实验表明小规模碰撞低，接近几何堆积极限时碰撞陡增，但协调与凝聚仅缓降而非崩溃，且安全与有序可兼得。
papers.abstract_en: Coordinating many miniature robots in a confined arena, with no leader, central planner, or global map, is a core challenge for swarm robotics. As the swarm grows denser, collision avoidance becomes the limiting factor, and the number of safely coexisting robots depends on the formulation of the inter-robot safety constraint. We present a distributed predictive flocking controller in which each robot solves its own nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) problem, optimizing swarm cohesion and alignment costs, inter-robot and obstacle safety, and a task objective, while exchanging only predicted trajectories with local neighbors. Within this generalized controller architecture, solved in real time, we compare six barrier and control-barrier-function (CBF) safety formulations on a digital twin of an open-source vibration-driven bristlebot in a $0.64\,\mathrm{m^2}$ arena. A look-ahead discrete-time CBF performs best overall, with the fewest collisions and the widest inter-robot margins across nearly every swarm size tested. We deploy it on phototaxis, phototactic orbiting, and cohesion without a stimulus tasks, using swarm sizes starting from ten robots and up to the geometric packing limit. The swarm holds well: collisions stay low in small swarms, rising steeply as the packing limit approaches, while coordination and cohesion degrade gently rather than collapsing. The swarm is found not to trade safety for order, keeping both across the confined arena, with local alignment high at every swarm size.

papers.title_en: Preference-Guided Cooperation in Multi-Objective Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.evidence: 基于目标级信用分配的多智能体协作
papers.tldr: 多目标多智能体强化学习需同时处理协作与目标权衡，现有方法常将二者分离，复杂度高。本文提出目标级反事实信用分配，并设计MIRL静态与动态变体，用元梯度让智能体个体化地优先目标、团队层面优化系统目标，从而以多目标结构直接引导合作。多目标多粒子环境实验显示，方法提升Pareto前沿质量，动态变体表现最强。该工作表明多目标结构可成为促进协作的可用信号。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-objective multi-agent reinforcement learning (MOMARL) addresses agent coordination and objective trade-offs simultaneously while optimising overall system performance. Existing work tends to treat multi-agent cooperation and multi-objective optimisation as largely independent components of a learning problem, which amounts to an exorbitant complexity except in trivial cases. We study here whether the structure provided by multiple objectives can itself be exploited to facilitate cooperation, rather than being treated as an additional optimisation challenge. We formulate MOMARL at both the team and individual levels and introduce objective-wise counterfactual credit assignment to evaluate each agent's contribution across the team objectives. We propose Meta-Gradient Informed Multi-Objective Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MIRL), with static (MIRL-S) and dynamic (MIRL-D) variants. By incorporating meta-gradient information, MIRL enables agents to learn how to prioritise objectives individually while collectively optimising the system-level objective, allowing the multi-objective structure to directly guide cooperation. Experiments on a multi-objective multiple particle environment show that our methods improve Pareto-front quality over baselines, with the dynamic variant achieving the strongest performance.

papers.title_en: Concurrent Task Orchestration: Hierarchical Trusted Collaborator Group Formation for Constrained Resource Allocation
papers.authors: Jiazhi Chen, Xianbin Wang, Xuemin "Sherman" Shen
papers.evidence: 面向多机协作的可信协作者分组与资源分配
papers.tldr: 面向资源受限无人机等移动智能机器的并发任务协作，现有方法难以兼顾有限分布式资源、动态协作者可用性与子任务依赖。论文提出可信协作者组形成与资源分配框架，将任务分解为子任务，构建统一价值—风险任务效用模型，并用分层匹配先粗聚类再细粒度组队分配。方法结合时空GNN信任预测与公平感知DRL持续更新匹配策略。仿真显示资源约束下并发任务完成性能较代表性基线提升22%，为并发任务编排提供可信协作与公平资源分配新思路。
papers.abstract_en: Effective collaboration among resource-constrained mobile intelligent machines, such as Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), is essential for the completion of complex tasks. However, concurrent task demands, limited distributed resources, and dynamic collaborator availabilities make it challenging to satisfy task-specific completion goals in diverse collaborative systems. To address these challenges simultaneously, we propose a new framework of trusted collaborator group formation and the supporting resource allocation strategy for concurrent task orchestration. Specifically, a collaborative task is decomposed into subtasks subject to dynamic resource availability and inter-subtask dependencies. A task utility model is developed for collaborator group evaluation support subtask allocation according to task completion goals and unified value-risk analysis. Based on this model, concurrent task orchestration is formulated as a long-term utility maximization problem under $α$-fairness. To solve the problem efficiently, we develop a hierarchical matching strategy that first clusters tasks and collaborators into coarse-grained sets and subsequently performs fine-grained collaborator group formation and task allocation within matched sets. Task-specific trust is predicted through spatial-temporal Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and embedded into a fairness-aware Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework to continuously update the matching policies. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy improves concurrent task completion performance by 22% over representative baselines under resource constraints.

papers.title_en: Collective Collaboration of Recursive Autonomous Agents
papers.authors: Ziqing Zhou, Linqiang Hu, Yuning Chen, Hongda Zhang, Zhao Huang, Ding Zhou, Haining Xu
papers.evidence: 面向智能工厂中递归自主智能体集体协作与协调的框架
papers.tldr: 智能工厂需跨设备、车间和工厂多尺度将订单目标转化为生产任务并协调变化，本文提出递归自主智能体集体协作框架。该框架以统一任务与能力接口支持目标自上而下递归分解、能力自下而上通过同伴协作聚合，使复合单元可作为同类智能体参与更高层组织。作者建立叶节点与复合单元组织模型，给出组合接口封闭性与有限任务展开条件，并设计任务分解、资源承诺、结果聚合与变更协调机制。跨车间机加、检测与物流网络案例表明，同一组织内核可在设备服务、车间和工厂尺度实例化。
papers.abstract_en: Smart factories must translate order-level objectives into production tasks at multiple scales and combine the capabilities of individual units into an overall delivery capability. To address repeated adaptation of organizational mechanisms across equipment, workshops, and factories, as well as coordination across levels under changing production conditions, this paper develops a framework for the collective collaboration of recursive autonomous agents (RAAs). A common task and capability interface supports the recursive decomposition of production objectives from the top down and the aggregation of conditional capabilities through peer collaboration from the bottom up. Composite units can therefore participate in higher-level organizations as agents of the same kind. We formulate organizational models for leaf and composite units, specify interface closure under composition and conditions for finite task expansion, and develop operational mechanisms linking task decomposition, resource commitments, result aggregation, and coordination within the scope affected by change. A production network integrating machining, inspection, and logistics across multiple workshops illustrates how a common organizational kernel is instantiated at the equipment-service, workshop, and factory scales. The framework connects recursive organization with explicit task responsibilities, capability conditions, and execution interfaces for manufacturing systems.

papers.title_en: Lightweight Change Detection for Adaptive Collective Perception in Dynamic Environments
papers.authors: Thiemen Siemensma, Tiago Travassos, Jiacheng Zhang, Bahar Haghighat
papers.evidence: 群体机器人在动态环境中集体感知并表征环境属性
papers.tldr: 群体机器人集体感知常假设环境静态，难以应对瓷砖比例与空间相关性随时间变化的动态场景。该工作将轻量变化检测嵌入贝叶斯集体决策，在检测到分布漂移时重置机器人信念，并在线调整采样间隔以缓解空间相关采样。Webots仿真显示变化检测延迟具竞争力，不同通信设置下精度更稳定，动态空间相关性下决策准确率提升。方法仅需常数内存与常数单样本计算，适合资源受限机器人。
papers.abstract_en: Swarm robotics enables scalable inspection through collective perception, where robots infer environmental properties from distributed observations. A common benchmark considers robots exploring black-white tiled environments and determining the majority tile type. While most work studies static environments, dynamic environments remain underexplored. We study collective perception in dynamic environments where the tile proportion and the spatial correlation of surface patterns may change over time. To enable implementation on resource-constrained robots, we integrate a lightweight change detection mechanism into a Bayesian collective decision-making framework that resets robot beliefs when distribution shifts are detected. The proposed detector requires constant memory and constant per-sample computation, unlike two recent competitive approaches that store the full sample stream, making it suitable for memory-constrained robots. We further introduce a method that detects spatially correlated sampling and adapts sampling intervals online to mitigate correlation effects. Our simulation results in Webots show competitive change detection delays, more consistent precision across communication settings, and improved decision accuracy under changing spatial correlations.

papers.title_en: IntNet: A Communication-Driven Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Cooperative Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Leandro Parada, Kevin Yu, Panagiotis Angeloudis
papers.evidence: 通信驱动的多智能体强化学习协同驾驶
papers.tldr: 多智能体强化学习在自动驾驶中受非平稳、部分可观测与协同不足制约，仅共享编码状态难以保障安全。IntNet将车辆意图传输与自适应通信调度统一到端到端MARL框架，用观测预测模块预测策略输出并经V2V共享，结合图注意力网络与调度器优化通信图。在城市混合交通中，它提升协同、降低碰撞，并将通信开销最多减少60%。该工作表明意图级通信与带宽感知调度可兼顾安全与效率。
papers.abstract_en: Achieving safety in autonomous driving through Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) is a critical yet challenging task due to non-stationarity, partial observability, and the need for effective coordination among agents. Although earlier cooperative MARL methods have aimed to improve coordination by sharing encoded state observations, we find these strategies are insufficient in safety-critical scenarios. To address this gap, we present IntNet, a novel MARL framework that enhances safety by incorporating the transmission of vehicle intent and adaptive communication scheduling into a unified end-to-end learning paradigm, jointly optimising all components for safe coordination. Central to our approach is an observation prediction module that enables agents to forecast subsequent policy outputs, which they can then share across a vehicle-to-vehicle network. Our model-free architecture employs a Graph Attention Network to process incoming messages and a scheduler component to dynamically optimise the communication graph for bandwidth efficiency. We compare IntNet against state-of-the-art communicative MARL methods in complex urban environments with both autonomous and human-operated vehicles, achieving improved coordination, lower collision rates, and reducing communication efforts by up to 60\%. Through extensive experiments, we assess the framework's learning efficiency, scalability, and the balance between information sharing and bandwidth usage for collision-free trajectories.

papers.title_en: PushAround: Collaborative Path Clearing via Physics-Informed Hybrid Search
papers.authors: Zili Tang, Zongyuan Li, Zishao Qiao, Meng Guo
papers.evidence: 移动机器人团队通过混合搜索协同清障
papers.tldr: 大型车辆在杂乱环境中常被可移动障碍阻断，移动机器人团队需清理可通行走廊。现有 NAMO 方法常抽象障碍位移，忽略机器人尺寸、质量、接触几何与力，易产生物理不可行计划。PushAround 将几何连通性推理与短时域仿真耦合，借助重复 WCCG 查询定位需拓宽的前沿间隙并按下游成本排序，生成直接或递归推障候选。实验验证 WCCG 与标准连通性检查一致，并展示更密杂乱场景、最多四机器人团队及物理参数失配下的鲁棒性。
papers.abstract_en: Large vehicles in cluttered environments are often blocked by movable obstacles, motivating mobile robot teams to clear traversable corridors. Navigation Among Movable Obstacles (NAMO) approaches often abstract obstacle displacements while neglecting robot dimensions, obstacle mass, contact geometry and forces, yielding physically infeasible plans. PushAround is a physics-informed hybrid search that couples geometric connectivity reasoning with short-horizon simulation to construct executable clearing plans. Repeated W-clearance connectivity graph (WCCG) queries expose frontier gaps requiring widening and rank them by estimated downstream costs. The search generates direct or recursive pushing candidates, selecting obstacles, directions, contacts and forces, and admits physics-evaluated candidates. Numerical experiments validate WCCG against standard connectivity checks and demonstrate scaling to denser clutter and teams of up to four robots, with robustness to simulated execution-side physical-parameter mismatch.
